item.title: Setting Up a Test for Two Study Methods
item.stimulus: A teacher believes that students who study with flashcards earn a greater mean exam score than students who study by rereading notes. At a school of 400 students, 200 study with flashcards and 200 study by rereading. A counselor independently and randomly selected 14 of the students who study with flashcards (sample mean 84.3 points, standard deviation 6.2) and 16 of the students who study by rereading (sample mean 79.8 points, standard deviation 7.0). Dotplots of both samples show no strong skewness and no outliers.

parts.prompt: Define the parameters of interest and state the null and alternative hypotheses for the test.

criteria.text: Defines μ₁ and μ₂ as the μ₁ is the true mean exam score, in points, of all students at the school who study with flashcards, and μ₂ is the true mean exam score of all students at the school who study by rereading notes.
criteria.evidence: Response defines μ₁ and μ₂ as the μ₁ is the true mean exam score, in points, of all students at the school who study with flashcards, and μ₂ is the true mean exam score of all students at the school who study by rereading notes, naming the response variable and the population in context.
criteria.fix: Name the parameter with its symbol and say which population mean (or mean difference) it is, in context.

criteria.text: States H₀: μ₁ − μ₂ = 0 and Hₐ: μ₁ − μ₂ > 0.
criteria.evidence: Response writes H₀: μ₁ − μ₂ = 0 and Hₐ: μ₁ − μ₂ > 0, with the alternative in the correct direction.
criteria.fix: Write the null with an equals sign and take the direction of the alternative from the question being investigated.

parts.prompt: Identify the appropriate procedure and show that its conditions are met.

criteria.text: Identifies the appropriate procedure as a two-sample t-test for a difference in population means.
criteria.evidence: Response names a two-sample t-test for a difference in population means.
criteria.fix: Name the procedure from the data design: one sample, matched pairs (analyze the differences), or two independent samples.

criteria.text: Checks the randomization condition: the students were selected by independent random samples from the two groups of students.
criteria.evidence: Response states the randomization condition in context: the students were selected by independent random samples from the two groups of students.
criteria.fix: Check that the data came from random selection or random assignment, and say how, in context.

criteria.text: Checks the 10% condition: each sample is less than 10% of its group of 200 students (14 and 16 are each under 20).
criteria.evidence: Response checks that the sample size is less than 10% of the population: each sample is less than 10% of its group of 200 students (14 and 16 are each under 20).
criteria.fix: When sampling without replacement, compare each sample size with 10% of its population to confirm independence.

criteria.text: Checks the sample-data condition: both sample sizes are less than 30, but the dotplots of both samples show no strong skewness and no outliers.
criteria.evidence: Response states the sample-data condition and why it is met: both sample sizes are less than 30, but the dotplots of both samples show no strong skewness and no outliers.
criteria.fix: State the condition that applies: sample sizes of at least 30, or samples with no strong skewness or outliers.

item.model_answer:
(a) Μ₁ is the true mean exam score, in points, of all students at the school who study with flashcards, and μ₂ is the true mean exam score of all students at the school who study by rereading notes. H₀: μ₁ − μ₂ = 0 versus Hₐ: μ₁ − μ₂ > 0.

(b) The procedure is a two-sample t-test for a difference in population means, Randomization: the students were selected by independent random samples from the two groups of students. 10% condition: each sample is less than 10% of its group of 200 students (14 and 16 are each under 20). Sample-data condition: both sample sizes are less than 30, but the dotplots of both samples show no strong skewness and no outliers.
item.verification_python:
n1, n2, m1, m2 = 14, 16, 84.3, 79.8
assert max(n1, n2) < 30
assert m1 > m2
print("ALL_CHECKS_PASSED")
